description: The Oracle legacy (+) outer-join operator, kept for Snowflake compatibility: a.x = b.y(+) in the WHERE of a COMMA join means a LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON a.x = b.y, and the table carrying the (+) is the NULL-SUPPLYING side. Putting the marker on the other operand flips which side is preserved. Conjuncts carrying (+) form the ON condition while the rest stay a RESIDUAL WHERE applied after the outer join - so a non-(+) filter removes a matched row without disturbing the null-extended one. Multiple keys each take their own (+), and the operator works in UPDATE ... FROM, where a target LEFT JOIN source updates every target row and leaves the source columns NULL for the unmatched ones. Converted 1:1 from query/OracleOuterJoinTest (now retired); the equivalence test compared two result sets row by row in a loop, so the converted test pins the ordered rows of both spellings.

CREATE TABLE t (c INTEGER, k INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10, 'x'), (1, 20, 'y')
CREATE TABLE m (c INTEGER, k INTEGER, w VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO m VALUES (1, 10, 'M')
SELECT t.v, m.w FROM t, m WHERE t.c = m.c(+) AND t.k = m.k(+) ORDER BY t.k
CREATE TABLE dest (k INTEGER, state VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO dest VALUES (1, '?'), (2, '?'), (3, '?')
CREATE TABLE mac (k INTEGER, cluster VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO mac VALUES (1, 'C1'), (2, 'C2')
UPDATE dest SET state = IFF(mac.cluster IS NULL, 'Deleted', 'Current') FROM mac WHERE dest.k = mac.k(+)
SELECT k, state FROM dest ORDER BY k
